Header:
Date: 2026-07-14 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jules (Redwood SE), Rina (CSM), Leo (Redwood SA), Tara (Aurelia VP Eng), Marco (NetOps), Priya (SRE), Evan (Security)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be noisy) ---
Samir: Quick sync to align on telemetry ingestion and routing playbook before we run the on-prem smoke test next week.

00:00 Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, um I know we had a couple of updates since last week so we'll go through telemetry first then the kernel upgrade plan then fallback routing, and leave 10 minutes for questions. Sound good?
00:18 Tara: yeah that works for us, thanks Samir. we got the README but we still need the clear list of metrics and the tag keys you expect.
00:27 Jules: right, and to be clear we send metrics via the forwarder — the agent — to the private control plane; a couple of fields might get mapped differently, so Marco we flagged the service name mapping in the doc.
00:42 Marco: okay I saw that, there was one mismatch in service name vs our internal name, that's easy to change. question on egress — do you need persistent peering or just outbound NAT?
00:56 Jules: for the smoke test we can do outbound NAT, but long-term we recommend a VPC peering for lower egress latency and more stable packets. for high-throughput inference the difference matters.
01:12 Priya: we saw the latency spikes in last week's run — at about 300ms — that correlated with a path change. did you have the fallback routing enabled?
01:24 Samir: yes we had a canary fallback, but I think the kernel we shipped on that node didn't have the newer NIC driver. so the KV cache warmup plus driver mismatch produced the spike.
01:38 Tara: driver mismatch, mm. so what's the plan for the upgrade window? we can't do heavy restarts in prime care hours.
01:48 Leo: agreed, so Jules and I sketched a staged kernel upgrade: drain, install, smoke test, quick rollback. We'll provide exact steps. also we included a checksum to verify the kernel/rt patch.
02:05 Jules: note that the upgrade includes an updated NIC firmware which we found reduces tail latency by about 12% in our lab — but it's vendor-specific. some transcribed i/o shows "N I C" as "nice" in the doc, ignore that.
02:22 Marco: firmware bump is sensitive for us; we prefer a canary on a non-prod rack. we can carve out a maintenance window next Tuesday 02:00-04:00 PT.
02:36 Samir: excellent. we'll treat that as target. Jules will put the playbook and rollback steps in the shared drive by Friday.
02:50 Tara: telemetry ingestion — how verbose? we can't leak PHI into metrics.
02:57 Rina: good point. Redwood's default telemetry strips PII and we can mask at source. but we'll send the pseudonymization checklist.
03:10 Evan: from security: can you confirm logs are sent encrypted and stored only in the private plane? also need retention settings for audit.
03:21 Jules: yep TLS + mTLS are used for the forwarder. logs land in the private control plane; retention is configurable. we'll add the SOC2 artifacts to the pack.
03:37 Priya: about MTU — during the last run we saw fragmentation and packet reassembly that slowed token streaming. is there a recommended MTU and do we need jumbo frames?
03:48 Jules: recommended MTU 9000 helps if your interconnect supports JUMBO. if not, we recommend lowering the batching window and enabling small-packet optimization in the runtime. both are in the tuning doc.
04:05 Marco: our interconnect supports 9000, but some switches in core don't. we'll test end-to-end path MTU this week.
04:16 Samir: ok next, routing playbook. I'll hand to Jules to walk the fallback logic.
04:22 Jules: cool. so the idea is multi-tier fallback: route to local on-prem variant -> if latency SLO violated route to dedicated pool in region -> if capacity exhausted route to hosted with a transformed model (lower perf but cheaper). failover decisions are token-loss aware and use a rolling window.
04:40 Tara: are those automated or manual? we need final sign-off from platform for any automated outbound to hosted.
04:48 Jules: can be automated but we'll default to manual for your trial. the config is a single boolean in the policy file — we'll show.
04:58 Priya: what about cost leak? if we route to hosted accidentally, our billing team needs to be notified.
05:06 Samir: we can emit an alert and a cost tag in the event. Redwood Console can push a webhook to your cost center.
05:14 Tara: good. also how will you preserve session affinity when routing across variants?
05:21 Jules: we use a prefix-preserving KV cache sync and a session token that can be exchanged — there may be small cold starts but we minimize them by prefix caching and the runtime's hot-kernel lane. sometimes transcribed as "K V cash" in automated notes.
05:36 Marco: last time we had cold starts spiking when session affinity broke. what's the expected 95th p99 improvement after the kernel bump?
05:45 Leo: in our lab with your traffic shape we saw p95 go from 220ms -> 180ms and p99 drop by ~14%. that's model and quantization dependent though.
06:00 Tara: speaking of quantization, will you apply dynamic quantization on our private cluster or only on hosted?
06:08 Jules: we provide quantization profiles that you can opt into. for private pilot we recommend the 8-bit profile with per-channel calibration — it saves tokens cost but should be validated by your eval prompts.
06:20 Priya: ok we'll run an eval. can you share your eval harness and sample prompts?
06:25 Samir: yes, we'll put a small harness in the repo and a sample prompt set — note prompts might be sanitized in the sample.
06:32 [09:05] Rina: quick sidebar — we uploaded the SAML SSO setup guide earlier; Tara, did you get it?
09:12 Tara: yes got it. still need role mapping for read-only vs admin.
09:18 Rina: we'll send a suggested mapping template after this call.
09:25 Samir: back to telemetry — Jules, what are the minimal metrics we need for smoke?
09:31 Jules: request latency, host-level GPU utilization, kv-cache hit rate, batch size distribution, and egress errors. that should be enough for the first run.
09:41 Marco: about egress shaping: can you rate-limit per-tenant or only per-instance?
09:46 Jules: per-instance today, per-tenant is on the roadmap but not in the 1.0 pilot build. we can emulate per-tenant by tagging instances.
09:57 Priya: are there any known knobs that increase tail latency besides batching?
10:03 Jules: yes: large batch windows, suboptimal kernel for sequence length, and packet fragmentation. we'll include tuning notes.
10:14 Tara: let's talk about the smoke test checklist — what are the acceptance criteria?
10:19 Leo: acceptance: <100ms median for 512 token average traffic, p95 under your SLO threshold (you set it), no packet loss, successful telemetry export snapshot, and successful canary rollback validation.
10:34 Marco: one more infra question — for NAT vs peering, if we do peering will your control plane call back into our network? any inbound connections?
10:42 Jules: no inbound; control plane initiates over established mTLS connections from your forwarder. peering only reduces egress hops; we don't open inbound ports.
10:54 Evan: security question — data at rest on the control plane, is that AES-256 with KMS?
11:01 Jules: yes AES-256 and you can bring your own KMS / HSM in the private deployment. we'll show the integration doc.
11:12 Tara: ok good. two quick asks: can you provide the rollback script early and an example of the iptables rules you mentioned?
11:20 Samir: yep. Jules will post both.
11:24 Jules: I'll include iptables examples and a simple env var driven fallback so you can flip the boolean without redeploying.
11:30 Priya: about observability retention — what's the default retention? we don't want to keep verbose traces longer than 30 days until production sign-off.
11:38 Rina: defaults are 90 days for metrics, 30 for traces, but we can scope them via config for the pilot.
11:46 Tara: perfect. last piece — compliance pack. Evan needs SOC2 docs and the audit log schema.
11:54 Rina: we'll attach SOC2 summary and a sample audit-log JSON schema to the drive.
12:03 Samir: ok moving toward wrap — recap and next steps.
12:08 Samir: action items: Jules will publish kernel upgrade playbook and iptables rules; Samir will upload telemetry checklist and the sample harness; Marco will validate MTU path; Evan will send SOC questions; Rina will send SSO mapping template.
12:25 Tara: thanks all, next sync after the smoke test. do you want the 7/21 date locked now?
12:31 Samir: yes let's lock 7/21 10:00 PT for the smoke — I'll send calendar invite after the call.
12:38 Jules: one note, if we see a path MTU smaller than 1500 at any hop we recommend switching to small-packet optimization before the smoke test.
12:45 Marco: got it, we'll test tonight and report.
12:50 Samir: great. thanks everyone.
